source.title: Scaling transition from momentum stochastic gradient descent to plain stochastic gradient descent
source.authors: Kun Zeng; Jin-Lan Liu; Zhixia Jiang; Dongpo Xu

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out and training performance across optimizers using different datasets and an accuracy-based measure; the optimizer comparisons bear on V4.
record.gate_note: The optimizer tables report test accuracy, training accuracy and training loss. Rows below retain test and training accuracy for each optimizer and setting; training loss is omitted. Figure-only curves and hyperparameter sensitivity results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam, AMSGrad and AdaBound comparisons with an SGD-family comparator on image classification. These comparisons test V4, although baseline hyperparameters are default or empirical rather than systematically tuned. TSGD's superiority alone does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that combining a scaling transition from momentum SGD to plain SGD with a decreasing learning rate gives faster convergence, higher accuracy and good generalization in their experiments; they also report improved stability.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the authors' scaling-transition optimizer and compares it with several optimizers; reports benchmark accuracy rather than a controlled replication of the optimizer studies named in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Whether StepLR is used changes the relative optimizer results; CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 results differ between the with-StepLR and without-StepLR settings.

fits_no_version.finding: TSGD has the highest reported test accuracy in Tables 1–5; the study also reports convergence and stability advantages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A scaling transition from momentum SGD to plain SGD can improve benchmark performance relative to the tested optimizer recipes.

record.problems: The paper says it uses default or empirical hyperparameter values for other algorithms, and the comparisons use different learning-rate schedules depending on the setting. Reported results are optimal values over the iterative process; no uncertainty estimates are given.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss entries from Tables 1–5 are omitted; Figure 1 and plotted training curves are not extracted. The rows retained cover the reported test and training accuracy entries across all five optimizer tables.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on the same task, including local connectivity and initialization interventions.
Language benchmarks, systematic learning-rate tuning, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. TSGD switches from momentum SGD to plain SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to large batches.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: All table values match the supplied text. Results are optimal values selected during training, not necessarily final checkpoints or paired train/test measurements at one checkpoint. One seed and no uncertainty estimates are reported. Baseline hyperparameters are default or empirical, so these results do not establish rankings after systematic tuning. The adaptive-versus-NSGD ranking reverses when StepLR is introduced on both CIFAR datasets. Figure curves and training-loss entries are already declared omitted in rows_left_out; no additional missing result is required.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks; broader optimizer tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness and other measured properties tracking generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.reason: R1–R4 show Adam tied with NSGD at 0.9813 and only small deficits for AMSGrad (0.0002) and AdaBound (0.0016); R6–R9 all reach perfect training accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly tied NSGD while AMSGrad and AdaBound trailed slightly despite perfect training accuracy, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, ResNet18, without StepLR
relationships.reason: R11–R14 and R31–R34 show all three adaptive comparators outperforming NSGD; Adam's advantages are 2.37 and 4.76 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: All three adaptive comparators reportedly exceeded NSGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet18, Adam and AMSGrad with StepLR
relationships.reason: R21–R23 show Adam and AMSGrad below NSGD by 1.45 and 0.72 percentage points despite higher reported training accuracies in R26–R28.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam and AMSGrad test accuracies than NSGD despite higher training accuracies remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R21 and R24 show AdaBound slightly exceeding NSGD, 0.9466 versus 0.9456; the 0.10-point advantage has no uncertainty estimate.
relationships.display_finding: AdaBound reportedly slightly exceeded NSGD, but the comparison remains unverified and uncertainty was unreported.

relationships.reason: R41–R44 show Adam, AMSGrad and AdaBound below NSGD by 3.36, 2.41 and 1.21 percentage points; only AdaBound has higher training accuracy in R46–R49.
relationships.display_finding: The reported test-accuracy deficits for Adam, AMSGrad and AdaBound, with only AdaBound training better than NSGD, remain unverified.
